question: The task label matches (binary MCI vs cognitively normal) but the measurement channel does not: P-117 (correct PDF S1746809423008959, Aljalal et al.) uses resting-state EEG; P-6 (Pourramezan Fard et al., CBM 176 (2024) 108606; claim_b names P-11, a dedup stub of P-6) uses conversational-language transcripts from I-CONECT (speech or language channel). Condition 1 fails on channel.
metric: Same metric type (accuracy), but segment-level (P-117) vs subject-level (P-6).

figures.P-117: 99.81% accuracy (ensemble KNN, 11 NSGA-II channels; 99.51% all 19 channels), binary aMCI vs HC, 10-fold CV over 3660 ten-second segment feature vectors from 61 participants (29 aMCI/32 HC); no interval reported. Wilson 95% with n = 61 subjects: z^2/n = 0.06297; centre = (0.9981 + 0.03149)/1.06297 = 0.9686; half-width 0.0314; interval [0.937, 1.000].
figures.P-6: 85.16% subject-level accuracy (mean of 5 folds, fold SD 5.76; AUC 84.75%), 68 I-CONECT subjects, 5-fold CV with 20% of subjects held out per fold. No 95% interval reported. Wilson with n = 68: z^2/n = 3.8415/68 = 0.05649; centre = (0.8516 + 0.02825)/1.05649 = 0.8328; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.8516*0.1484/68 + 3.8415/(4*68^2))/1.05649 = 0.0843; interval [0.748, 0.917].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. Neither paper reports a result in the other's channel, and P-117 prints only segment-level accuracies (no subject-level figure under P-6's evaluation unit). Nothing reconciles the pair.
performance_validity: P-117 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on its own PDF: 99.81% (>= 0.97) from internal 10-fold CV that randomly splits the segment feature matrix (no subject-wise split described), 61 participants, no external cohort; the registry flag is false only because its Best_Metric is 'not reported'. P-6 (85.16%) is not excluded.
reason: The gap is numerically beyond uncertainty (0.9981 lies outside P-6's Wilson [0.748, 0.917] and 0.8516 lies outside P-117's [0.937, 1.000]), but the two studies measure different channels (EEG vs language transcripts), so they do not address the same clinical question under condition 1. P-117's figure also fails the performance-validity exclusion (condition 5). The record duplicates C-48 after the P-11 -> P-6 repoint; its figures are otherwise quoted correctly.

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method.
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.

For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets, with one subset used for validation (test) and the other nine for training
This results in a 3660 × 76 feature matrix, which is used as input to the classifier.
Since the number of available subjects in the I-CONECT dataset is 68, we assess the performance of our framework using the K-fold validation technique.
the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 85.16% and an AUC of 84.75%, with the corresponding std of 5.76 and 5.97, respectively.
